children.name: Thurnia polycephala
children.description: Thurnia polycephala Schnee — a helophytic (marsh) herb native to the Guayana Shield region of southeastern Colombia, southern Venezuela, and northern Brazil. Described by L. Schnee in 1943. Found at low elevations (around 90 m) in the Guiana Shield biogeographic region. Like other Thurnia species, it is a rush-like perennial monocot in the small relictual family Thurniaceae (order Poales). Predicted extinction risk: not threatened.

children.name: Thurnia sphaerocephala
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia to N. South America. It is a helophyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Thurnia jenmanii
children.description: Thurnia jenmanii Hook.f. — a subshrub in the family Thurniaceae, endemic to Guyana in northern South America. The type species of the genus Thurnia, first described by J.D. Hooker in 1883 based on specimens collected by G.S. Jenman along the Potaro River. Grows in the wet tropical biome. Part of a small relictual genus of rush-like herbaceous plants closely related to the Juncaceae within the order Poales.

children.name: Prionium serrata Buchenau, 1875
children.description: Prionium serrata Buchenau, 1875 — a taxonomic feminine-form variant of P. serratum (palmiet), the only species in the genus Prionium. A robust, evergreen, semiaquatic, rhizomatous monocot growing to 2 m tall, with stiff, leathery, grey-green lanceolate leaves with toothed margins and a high silica content. Endemic to South Africa (Western Cape to KwaZulu-Natal), where it grows in dense stands along streams and rivers on sandstone substrates, stabilizing riverbeds and preventing erosion. Small brown flowers in a branched inflorescence; fruit a dry dehiscent capsule. Young flower shoots are edible; leaves used for basketry.

children.name: Prionium serratum
children.description: Prionium serratum, the palmiet, is a robust, evergreen, semiaquatic, rhizomatous flowering plant growing to 2 m (6 ft 7 in) in height. It is the only species in the genus Prionium, and is endemic to South Africa (Cape Province and KwaZulu-Natal).
